wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Iran tightened its hold on the Strait of Hormuz: its navy says 2 supertankers hit mines, it blacklisted 26 tugs, and ship crossings fell more than 40% in three weeks. Its strikes reached an industrial site in Bahrain, a drone killed 2 Italian technicians in Kuwait, and US envoy Jared Kushner confirmed meetings with Iranian officials.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: Iran's Guard says two tankers hit mines in Hormuz and burned, and the Houthis told workers at Jeddah's port to evacuate. OPEC+ is leaning toward rolling quotas into January because the Iran war makes 2027 targets impossible to set, while Iraq, after $8.8 billion in October crude revenue, wants a higher quota.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The slide was a glut story: Brent fell to a three-month low as supply outran demand, even while mines hit tankers off Khasab. The rebound came as Iran's Guard said two more tankers burned in Hormuz, Ukrainian drones cut Russian refining 45%, and the Houthis said they attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: A mine struck an LNG carrier in Hormuz, and a week later only 2 liquefied natural gas tankers crossed the strait, stranding most of Qatar's cargoes. The IMF now sees Qatar's economy shrinking more than 14%. Buyers short of that gas bid for US supply instead, and in the UK Ofgem raised the price cap 26% from January.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: Nothing reported this month reaches back to the price through September. Since then, a wheat ship capsized off Bulgaria after a reported sea-drone strike, and Black Sea strikes now threaten the route that supplied Egypt's 9.44 million tons this year. Wheat sowing in India trails last year by 15.3%.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: After the last monthly reading, copper fell below $12,000 in London on a 9% weekly drop, its third-biggest in a decade, amid doubts about data-centre demand. Supply is shifting: Congo is closing on Chile as top supplier, and in New Delhi, Adani agreed to buy 2,000 tons of recycled copper anode monthly.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: The Fed is now debating rate rises, not cuts: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, beating forecasts, and the minutes showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes. Goolsbee left a larger-than-usual rise open for December, though CME FedWatch later priced zero chance of a half-point move, and yields held up even as oil fell.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The chipmakers that had carried the index dragged it down: Nvidia shed $2.74 trillion in value amid an accounting probe and AI doubts, and Anthropic's IPO faded after its debut. Trump then readied tariffs on 16 economies, China among them, and the selling reached Asia, where the Taiex fell as much as 7.9%.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: An AI selloff through Micron, TSMC and ASML cut the Nasdaq 5.28% on one Friday, days after Anthropic raised a record $81.3bn in its listing there and then tumbled more than 10%. Nvidia added nearly $1 trillion when its board reinstated Jensen Huang, before halting chip shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia under a new US licence rule.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The fortnight's fuel news came from outside the US. Ukrainian drones cut Russian refining 45%, and Pakistan trimmed pump prices with Brent near $96 on the Iran war. None of it accounts for the fall at US pumps.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Qatari LNG, which European buyers compete for, is barely leaving the Gulf. A carrier exploded on a mine in Hormuz, only 2 tankers crossed the strait in one week, and the IEA says $40bn of pipelines will not end the Gulf's Hormuz dependence. A cold snap spreading across the region has since added heating demand.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: Nvidia fell into a leadership crisis after Jensen Huang's exit, even as it forecast $130 billion in Q4 revenue, and the Middle East's new US AI pact was signed under that cloud. A week later US inflation rose further in October, hotter than expected, alongside fresh tariffs, and stocks closed mixed.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight's Pakistani economic news ran through oil and the IMF. Oman lent Pakistan State Oil $200m for fuel, petrol was cut to Rs313 a litre, and the cabinet ended sugar export subsidies and price controls to meet an IMF benchmark. None of it accounts for the rupee's small drift.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: The slide was put down to election risk: Tinubu is campaigning, and in Delta gunmen killed 4 supporters of Ovie Omo-Agege's campaign, prompting the Nigeria Democratic Congress to boycott police security talks. In Abuja, an investigator testified that Emefiele recoloured the naira rather than redesigning it, the change behind the 2023 cash crunch.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: IMF staff agreed to release $2.3bn to Egypt, and Cairo set aside 112 million square metres of coast to cut its debt and began paying on the spot for miners' gold, three ways of raising hard currency. Against them, strikes in the Black Sea threatened the route for the 9.44 million tons of wheat Egypt has bought there since January.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: The fortnight's Turkish economic news was gold falling 6.4% in 7 days to $3,853 an ounce, which thinned the cushion households keep against the lira. The Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline also pumped crude again after a decade. None of it accounts for the lira's own path.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The fortnight in Dhaka was political. Arsonists hit 37 Grameen Bank branches from 10 November, the home of Muhammad Yunus was set on fire, paramilitary units were deployed, and Sheikh Hasina named December 16 for her return from exile in India. Nothing in that reporting ties any of it to the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: Indonesia's news over the fortnight was a flooded illegal gold mine in Bogor, a factory fire in Serang, Prabowo meeting Xi in Shenzhen and a court ruling against the 1997 Military Justice Law. None of it accounts for the currency's slide.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight in Lebanon brought an army raid that seized a large weapons depot in Beirut, and a revival of Liban Telecom, a state company that had existed only on paper since 2005. None of it reached the pound, which stays where the central bank holds it.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: The fortnight's news out of China was about companies, not the currency: Vanke asking bondholders for a second extension and CATL's market value falling below a trillion yuan. Nothing in it explains the yuan's path against the dollar.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: Foreign investors put nearly $15 billion into Indian stocks in November, and the dollars they sold to buy in lifted the rupee to an eight-month high. That held as the Fed turned hawkish and the Trump administration readied new tariffs; the weak point is oil, since India imports most of its crude and the Iran war has kept Brent high.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The real's weakest day was the one on which Brasília cut its 2027 growth forecast and raised expected inflation to 4.5% against a 3.0% target, while Galipolo, a Lula appointee, said the minimum wage feeds inflation. US tariff proposals on aircraft and sugar came later in the week, and Lula's office called them unacceptable.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: Mexico's news in these weeks was the arrest of El Chapo Isidro, the Sinaloa leader on the FBI's most wanted list, in a shoot-out that left eleven dead, and Sheinbaum's push for talks with US aviation authorities over SpaceX debris in Tamaulipas. Neither accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: Washington sold $500 million of euros to buy yen as the yen breached 160. The ECB left France to the markets as its borrowing premium over Germany hit 1.75 points, and euro zone output held at 51.7 only because Germany surged while France contracted. Then Pablo Hernández de Cos beat Dutch hawk Klaas Knot to succeed Lagarde at the ECB.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Washington sold $500 million of euros to buy yen after the currency breached 160. The weakness is squeezing the Finance Ministry's 50-60 trillion yen defence plan, and Tokyo core inflation hit 2.9%, the fastest since July 2025, hardening the case for a December Bank of Japan rate hike.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: The fortnight's news on Russia was military and diplomatic rather than monetary: Ukrainian drones cut Russian refining 45% and Putin vowed retaliation, OPEC+ weighed rolling its quotas into January, and Brussels drafted a sanctions package aimed at Russian sport. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: In the fortnight, South Africa held rates at 7.25%, with 3 of 7 rate-setters voting to hike, and a court voided the report that had revived Ramaphosa's impeachment. Neither accounts for the rand's weakening, and a near-hike would ordinarily have pulled it the other way.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: Fed hikes and a tech selloff pulled money out of the exchange-traded funds that hold bitcoin, and BlackRock's fund posted a record $541 million outflow. A China tariff threat then knocked it back below $60,000. Strategy's enterprise value fell below the worth of its 851,305 bitcoin, and BTCS warned it could not rule out liquidation of a $54 million loan.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Ethereum fell with the wider crypto selloff: Bitcoin dropped below $65,000 and then $60,000, and spot bitcoin ETFs headed for their biggest monthly outflow on record. On its own network, developers counted 15,000 contracts at risk from the Glamsterdam upgrade and delayed it to 2027, before clearing it for a December test.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: Hot US inflation data made Federal Reserve rate hikes likely, and higher real yields raise the cost of holding a metal that pays nothing; an AI selloff deepened it into gold's worst week since March. Street buyers went the other way: Dubai's souq chased the dip and Karachi dealers ran short of bars, charging up to Rs30,000 extra per tola.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: On Tuesday an air raid alert sent 8,700 islanders on Ulleungdo toward shelters over Russian aircraft. That came a day after Ukraine said 7 naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury off Benghazi, and days after 2 missiles and a drone fell on southeast Poland, which Warsaw blamed on Russia.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Tankers have been hitting mines and projectiles in Hormuz and off Khasab, and Iran blacklisted 26 tugs, some registered in the UAE, India and Singapore. Ship crossings fell more than 40% in three weeks, Iran struck a Bahraini industrial site, and Oman is lending Pakistan State Oil $200m for fuel.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Tankers kept hitting mines: Iran's navy said two supertankers struck them on 23 November, and Iran's Guard reported two more burning two days later. Tehran also blacklisted 26 tugs, some registered in the UAE, India and Singapore, and crossings fell more than 40% in three weeks while Doha pushed to revive Iran-US talks.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Yemeni government forces withdrew from the strait's shore and left the Houthis in control, then the Houthis pressed on toward Aden. The same week a Japanese container ship transited for the first time in three years, and 22 countries' coastguards agreed to patrol the Red Sea jointly, while Houthi strikes turned on Riyadh and Ras Tanura.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Carriers began testing the route again: a Japanese container ship transited Bab al-Mandab after three years away, and 22 countries' coastguards agreed to patrol the Red Sea jointly. Then the Houthis told workers at Jeddah's port to evacuate and said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, the threat that keeps most lines off the canal.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from elsewhere: mines struck tankers in Hormuz, where crossings fell more than 40% in three weeks. Nvidia also stopped server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. Neither accounts for traffic through this strait.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The fortnight's news from around the strait was about trade and chips, not shipping: Washington readied new tariffs on 16 economies, Alibaba's Apex unit joined the US export blacklist and the Taiex fell as much as 7.9%. None of it reached the vessels passing through.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: The fortnight's news from the region was about drought wrecking harvests in Honduras and Guatemala, and Etesa transmission contracts in Panama City that quadrupled in cost. None of it bears on the ships moving through the canal.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: In mid-November, drones hit 3 ships inside Romanian waters, and a wheat ship capsized off Bulgaria after a reported sea-drone strike; all 12 crew survived. These were strikes on the grain trade that leaves the Black Sea through this strait. Egypt has taken 9.44 million tons of Black Sea wheat since January and is directly exposed.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The nearest shipping news was a cargo ship carrying more than a million litres of diesel that sank off Ibiza. That came after the latest reading and far inside the Mediterranean, so nothing reported explains the traffic.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Two things thinned the route at once. Tankers hit mines and burned off Khasab, and crossings of Hormuz fell more than 40% in three weeks, which leaves fewer Gulf cargoes to make the long run around Africa. A Japanese container ship also transited Bab al-Mandab for the first time in three years, an early sign of lines returning to the Red Sea.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge over the strait repeatedly within days. Drones came first, then a second strike within 24 hours dropped the road span, and satellite imagery showed at least two hits on the rail span. None of the reporting says the shipping channel beneath it was closed.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The fortnight's Turkish news ran to COP31 in Antalya ending without a deal, the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline pumping crude again and a defence pact with Qatar. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The Nvidia scandal reached Kuala Lumpur this month. Scrutiny fell on the data centres behind $94.67 billion of investment that Malaysia's trade ministry has approved since 2021, Washington tightened AI-chip rules, and Nvidia stopped server shipments to Malaysia. Trump is also readying new tariffs on 16 economies.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: The fortnight in Indonesia brought a candy factory fire in Serang, a flooded illegal gold mine near Bogor, a court order to amend the 1997 Military Justice Law, Prabowo's meeting with Xi in Shenzhen and Nvidia halting server shipments to Indonesia. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The yen breached 160 and Washington sold $500 million of euros to buy it, while core inflation, 2.2% nationally and then 2.9% in Tokyo, cemented a Bank of Japan rate hike. After the low, the US proposed sweeping new tariffs on China and others, and Japan's private sector growth slowed to a six-month low.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The trough came as Asian chip stocks sold off on AI doubts, with Taiwan's Taiex down as much as 7.9% on Wednesday. Big listings reported a weak quarter: Xiaomi's phone shipments fell 29% as memory costs rose, Kuaishou's revenue fell 11.1%, and Tencent's capital spending jumped 528% under chip curbs.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The trough fell on the day Shanghai's party secretary Chen Jining, a Politburo member, came under investigation, as Vanke asked bondholders for a second extension. CATL lost a large share of its value after a reported production cut, and Trump readied tariffs on 16 economies including China.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Doubts about AI spending hit the two chipmakers that carry the index. Samsung and SK Hynix led a Kospi drop of more than 5% in one session, and the rout spread to Asian chip stocks, with Taiwan's Taiex falling as much as 7.9%. In the same week, Trump readied new tariffs on 16 economies.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: Foreign investors put nearly $15 billion into Indian stocks in November, enough to lift the rupee to an eight-month high. They bought even with retail inflation at a two-year high of 6.09% in October and the Trump administration set to unveil new tariffs on India. Exports had jumped 30% that month.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's fortnight was dominated by the US crackdown on chip diversion: Megaspeed faced a criminal probe, Alibaba's Apex unit joined the export blacklist, and Nvidia stopped server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. None of it touches the banks and property firms that carry the index, or accounts for its fall.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fall was a chipmaker sell-off. On Wednesday the Taiex dropped as much as 7.9% in a single session as Asian chip stocks plunged, and an index this heavy in TSMC goes wherever the region's semiconductor shares go.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Australia's annual inflation reached 4.9% despite 125 basis points of hikes, and firms said they expect it to hold over 4% for the next 12 months, a backdrop that bears on the banks weighing heaviest in the index. Neither report explains the slide, which began before the inflation figure was published.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The trough came the day after the Reserve Bank held its repo rate at 7.25%, with 3 of 7 rate-setters voting to hike as inflation risks widened, which kept South African borrowing costs high. Within a week a court voided the report that had revived Ramaphosa's impeachment, removing a political risk hanging over the government.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Brasília cut its growth forecast and now expects 4.5% inflation against a 3.0% target, and Galipolo tied the minimum wage to rising prices, a case for keeping rates high. The US then proposed a 10% duty on Brazilian aircraft and on sugar. Embraer sank, and Lula's office called the proposals unacceptable.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The news out of Mexico in these weeks was the capture of Sinaloa kingpin El Chapo Isidro, in a shoot-out that left eleven dead, and Sheinbaum's push for US talks over suspected SpaceX debris falling in Tamaulipas. Neither accounts for the index's move.

mkt:byma.standing: Argentina's main stock index, on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos in Buenos Aires. Priced in pesos, which have repeatedly lost most of their value, so it rises even in bad years: daily direction counts, the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: Argentina appears to have entered recession after two shrinking quarters, a fresh blow to Milei's economic policy that came with growing job concerns. Those figures were published after the index's slide, not before it, and nothing else in the fortnight's news from Buenos Aires accounts for the fall.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: The trough came the week US sour crude's war premium vanished as supply surged, a weight on an index this heavy in oil producers. Ties with Washington soured alongside it: Carney said only US policy shifts could change Canada's trade stance, and days later the Pentagon restricted military cooperation with Canada.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Nvidia carried the late-November bounce: Jensen Huang's return as CEO sent its stock up nearly 31%, adding nearly $1 trillion in a day. Pulling the other way, October inflation reached 3.8%, strengthening the case for a Fed hike, and Trump readied new tariffs on 16 economies.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The fortnight brought UK inflation still above target after more than two years, copper's 9% weekly drop, a 26% rise in Ofgem's price cap and Poundland's slide into administration, but none of it is tied to this index's fall or its rebound.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Deutsche Bank shares dropped after a leak of 15 million files exposed its compliance failures, and Lufthansa cut 1,000 jobs over fuel costs. Neither accounts for a slide across the whole index. Euro zone figures showed Germany's output surging while the index fell.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: French assets carried a political and fiscal discount: France's borrowing premium over Germany hit 1.75 points as the ECB left France to markets, and Ifop put Le Pen at 32-36% with the centre stalled. Business output in France contracted while Germany surged. Sanofi, one of the index's heaviest members, offered $41bn for Insmed.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: In Veldhoven, ASML's chief executive argued that export controls on China backfire, saying the company holds close to 100% of China's market. Nothing in the news ties that, or Klaas Knot losing the ECB race to Pablo Hernández de Cos, to the index's slide.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The fortnight in Madrid was political: Sánchez admitted 'mistakes' 10 days before elections, a debate poll had Feijóo winning, and euro countries picked Pablo Hernández de Cos as the next ECB president. None of the reporting ties any of it to Spanish share prices.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Rome wants €5.9 billion from Italy's banks next year, and Intesa publicly attacked the levy. Banks are the index's heaviest weight. UniCredit, the other giant, won unconditional EU approval for its €45 billion bid for Commerzbank and now plans to put its own chief executive atop the German lender.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The fortnight's Swiss market news was the franc being bid up as a haven during the AI selloff, and an SNB vice president telling Le Matin Dimanche that Swiss inflation has been accelerating. Neither is reported as moving the index itself.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The fortnight turned on who governs Israel: Likud and Yashar ended coalition talks over Itamar Ben-Gvir, Gadi Eisenkot then signed the Democrats to a bloc of 48 of 120 seats, and judges told prosecutors a Netanyahu bribery conviction is unlikely. None of those reports ties the turns to share prices.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The late-month events came after the early peak and do not account for it: in Shenzhen, Trump joined Xi and Putin in a peace declaration that names no war. At home he barred federal contractors from answering Congress without permission, told the Justice Department to expedite federal executions and demanded an investigation into a 4.3% GDP revision.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: October's inflation reading of 3.8%, from the Bureau of Economic Analysis, and an upgrade to US GDP figures kept a December rise in play. CME FedWatch shows zero chance of a half-point hike, so the bets are on a smaller step. The prospect of more hikes pushed gold to a 14-month low and helped drive bitcoin below $60,000.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: None of the fortnight's news explains the rate itself; the story was who sets it next. Pablo Hernández de Cos beat Dutch hawk Klaas Knot to succeed Christine Lagarde, Germany took the chief economist seat for Markus Brunnermeier, and the bank left France's borrowing premium over Germany to markets at 1.75 points.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: Silver fell with gold, which had its worst week since March as traders bet the Fed would raise rates and an AI selloff hit markets. Gold lost 8.9% that week and touched its lowest since September 2025, and by the window's end it was rebounding from that one-year low as AI jitters eased.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: The Fed's preferred gauge, the PCE price index from the Bureau of Economic Analysis, reached 3.8% in October, rising 0.3% on the month after 0.5% in September, which cemented a quarter-point rate rise in December. Inside the Fed the split is over the cause: tariffs and the Iran-war energy shock, or demand.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Kyiv carried the war far from the front: Ukraine says 7 naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury off Benghazi, and that it damaged 5 aircraft at the Savasleyka airbase east of Moscow. Washington wants a peace deal by January 2027, and the EU proposed a €45 billion loan that Ukraine repays only if Russia pays reparations.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.
xmr.recent: The fortnight's ransomware stories, Ukraine's arrest of 4 suspects in a $40.5 million scheme and the attack that halted radiation therapy at Guadeloupe's largest hospital, never say which coin the ransoms were paid in, and none of them accounts for the fall in the price.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Jensen Huang's exit amid a spy scandal, followed by an SEC accounting probe that crashed chip stocks, drove the slide. The board reinstated Huang and the stock rose nearly 31%; within days Nvidia stopped server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia under a new US rule requiring licences for buyers there.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple's own news in the fortnight was an outage it blamed on an internal update, reports that its first smart glasses are taking shape, and a move into AI agents that control the device while raising new barriers for competitors. None of it accounts for the share's climb.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: The news about Google's own business was product news. It shipped Gemini Neon, its fourth Gemini 4 model in 7 weeks. It redesigned its homepage, dropping the Search button for 3 AI buttons. It also set a rule blocking Android apps from unregistered developers from January 2027. None of it accounts for the fall in the share.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon's own news was mostly its Leo satellite network: a United Launch Alliance Vulcan failure destroyed 40 of its satellites, an Ariane 6 lifted 36 more, and it turned to SpaceX for launches. The FAA also opened a probe into a delivery drone crash. None of it explains the share's slide.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.
co:tsmc.recent: The one story about the company's own business was a TSMC unit asking Brazos County, Texas, for a property tax limit on a proposed $22.6bn fab, and nothing in it accounts for the fall in the share price.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Outlook and Teams went down for nearly a day, and the shares fell 3% as the disruption spread. The same week a researcher leaked SignDrop, a Windows exploit that gives ordinary users System rights. Microsoft has since declared a Code Red over a 24-hour outage that hit governments in Canada, the US, Australia and Japan.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: SpaceX laid out $74 billion of AI computing campuses, caught Ship 42 on the tower after 14 orbits, and won a US licence for 1 million satellites. Virginia and Oregon sued it over Grok, and Musk pledged two shares for every US child. None of it is reported as moving the share price.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Italy fined Meta $880m over photo privacy, Germany's consumer federation sued it over its Ray-Ban Meta camera glasses, and protesters stormed its Hyderabad office over withheld opposition Instagram accounts. None of it touches the advertising business the share price rests on, and none of it accounts for the price.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: The Yemeni military named Aramco its prime target in Saudi Arabia, a threat aimed at the company's own installations rather than at the oil market. Nothing reported in the period ties that threat to a strike or explains the share price.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Bloomberg reported that SpaceX and Tesla were in merger talks aimed at an announcement in December. A day later Tesla opened Cybercab orders to select customers for personal use, the robotaxi's first step toward private buyers. Then Italy approved Tesla's driver assistance before any EU vote on it.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: It fell with Asia's chipmakers as doubts about AI spread to the companies that supply its memory: Samsung and SK Hynix dragged the Kospi down more than 5%, and days later the Taiex fell as much as 7.9%. The one piece of Samsung's own business news was a deal, not a result: buyout talks with Modine.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: In Washington, Commerce licensed AMD and Nvidia chips for sale to military-listed Chinese firms, a ruling on where the company may sell. The licences came after most of the share's slide, and nothing in the input accounts for the fall itself.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: The bank's own news was operational. Nearly 5,000 Chase customers reported outages on a Monday, Downdetector counted, the third disruption in a week, with Zelle transfers delayed too. Days later, hackers took customer data through a vendor shared with Visa and Mastercard. Neither event explains a slide that began weeks earlier.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: Doubts about AI spending fell hardest on the chipmakers selling into it: SK Hynix and Samsung dragged the Kospi down more than 5%, and the selloff spread across Asia, with the Taiex falling as much as 7.9% on Wednesday. It landed as SK Hynix raced to finish its first fab at Yongin, a plant 150 metres tall.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: The one story about the company's own business was a departure at Flipkart, Walmart's Indian e-commerce arm: chief executive Kalyan Krishnamurthy leaves on 4 December, 9 days after the announcement, ending 11 years in the job. The news arrived after the share had already done its climbing, and nothing in the input accounts for the rise.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: The one story about the company in this stretch was its CEO arguing against decoupling: he said ASML holds close to 100% of China's market and made the case for continuing to sell to China despite export controls. Nothing in that account explains the fall in the share.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.
us-mortgage.recent: The one related story in the fortnight reported US home sales at their lowest level since 2016. That is what high borrowing costs do to buyers, but it does not explain why the rate itself rose.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.
ez-cpi.recent: The only related story was about who leads the euro area's central bank, not about prices: Pablo Hernández de Cos beat Dutch hawk Klaas Knot for the job. Nothing reported explains the rise in inflation.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: Solana slid with bitcoin, which fell below $65,000 for the first time since August and kept going to a two-year low before bouncing 9% to retake $60,000 ahead of Monday's stock open. In the same days, VanEck dropped Gemini as custodian of its bitcoin, ether and SOL ETFs.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: The one story in this window about the venue itself was a guilty plea from a former Robinhood engineer over an insider trading scheme run on Hyperliquid. Nothing in it explains the token's slide.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: Two of Zcash's main developers urged holders to move about $300 million of ZEC out of the older Sapling shielded pool before advances in mathematics make it breakable. No working attack has been shown, and the newer Ironwood pool avoids the technique at issue. The warning came at the end of the slide and does not account for most of it.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: UK inflation accelerated to 3.6% in October, leaving it above target for more than two years. The Bank of England's chief economist said further rate rises were needed to combat it, and Pill later argued that action was needed to maintain inflation credibility.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: Core prices in Tokyo rose 2.9% in November, the fastest since July 2025, while a hawkish Bank of Japan member pressed for quick rate hikes. National core inflation hit 2.2% in October, below the 2.3% forecast, but it was still read as cementing the next hike.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The fortnight's news carried the PBOC holding the yuan's daily fix stable as volatility jumped after APEC, and Singapore and China agreeing to deepen yuan ties with a focus on corporates. Neither touched the rate itself.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.
bcb-rate.recent: The fortnight carried one relevant story: in Brasília, Galipolo, a Lula appointee, argued that the minimum wage feeds inflation, the pressure that keeps a central bank wary of easing. It says nothing about the decisions behind the rate's path, and does not account for where it now sits.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.
bi-rate.recent: The rupiah fell to a record low against the dollar in mid-November as bets on the Fed lifted the US currency. A weak rupiah is the pressure this rate is used to answer.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia's news this fortnight was about its reserves, not its rate: gold holdings fell to a 7-year low, and it kept buying yuan in settlements on November 13 and November 25, none of which accounts for the cuts.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The trough came on the day Nvidia stopped server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, which put the region's data centre build-out in question. The same day, an explosion at an oil depot in Bangkok's Phra Khanong district injured seven people. Neither event accounts for the longer slide that came before them.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Since mid-November the Houthis have carried the Yemen war onto Saudi soil: missiles at King Khalid Airport, the PIF tower in Riyadh hit twice in 5 days, a strike on the Ras Tanura refinery and an order to evacuate Jeddah's port. The index's slide and its October trough came before that campaign, and none of it accounts for them.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The final session's jump came as Dubai Islamic Bank agreed to buy Emirates Islamic from Emirates NBD entirely with new shares, creating the UAE's largest Islamic lender, with state-linked Dubai owners behind both banks. Nothing else in the fortnight's news, the gold price drop or Iran's Hormuz blacklist among it, explains the earlier climb.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Manila's fortnight was diplomatic: Trump announced a trade deal with the Philippines and new critical-mineral deals at the Quad, and Marcos left for APEC in Shenzhen. None of it was reported as reaching listed Philippine companies, and nothing in the input accounts for the index's slide.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: The slide began the day after Italy fined Meta $880m over photo privacy, and ran through a week in which Jason Wei, a chain-of-thought author, quit Meta's TBD Lab. Hamburg regulators then found the recording light on Ray-Ban Meta glasses hard to see, and Germany's consumer federation sued over them.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.
poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.recent: Sánchez's head-to-head debate with Feijóo, fought over corruption and housing, went against him: an Ateneo del Dato poll found 45% thought Feijóo won and 32% Sánchez. None of the fortnight's reporting explains the brief rise in mid-November.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: Tencent's quarterly capital spending jumped 528% to 81.4 billion yuan, poured into AI it is giving away cheaply. Hy4 flash launched at $0.07 per million input tokens, cutting task costs by 95% in internal tests, and four days later the full 770-billion-parameter Hy4 was released as open weights anyone can download and modify.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Shares slid even after Nvidia doubled profit to $65.3 billion and forecast a $130bn quarter without Jensen Huang, then crashed with chip stocks on an accounting probe. They rose nearly 31% as Huang returned as CEO, before a US licence rule stopped server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Google dropped the Search button from its homepage in favour of 3 AI buttons, shipped Gemini Neon as its fourth Gemini 4 model in 7 weeks, and won a judge's approval to train AI on Spirit Airlines' emails, while four nonprofits sued to freeze its next models. None of it explains the fall in the share.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: The war widened instead of pausing: Houthis claimed missiles at King Khalid Airport, Saudi-led strikes on Hodeidah killed at least 9, and Riyadh sounded alerts a third night running. Then Ras Tanura refinery was hit and Houthis closed on Aden, while the Makkah pact met in Islamabad on whether Pakistan's pledge to Saudi defence becomes troops.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: Iran's foreign minister said its 60% uranium stockpile stays home, ruling out the handover this contract pays on, as Iranian strikes on Bahrain and mines in Hormuz hardened the standoff. The talks did not collapse: Doha is reviving them, and Jared Kushner confirmed meetings with Iranian officials through a channel run by Vance.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Venezuela's authorities formally schedule a national election before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on a vote being called, not on one being held.

poly-will-any-country-join-the-mecca-agr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if any further country formally joins the Mecca Agreement before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the pact widening beyond its founding signatories.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, envoys and sanctions decisions.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: The fighting widened rather than narrowed: Putin vowed 'much more painful' strikes, debris from a suspected Russian missile burned in a Polish field, and Ukraine hit the Savasleyka airbase and sank the corvette Merkury off Libya. Washington's own target for a peace deal is January 2027, after this contract closes.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no senior American and Iranian officials meet before 2026 ends. The two governments have met at that level only rarely since 1979, so a meeting would break a long pattern.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: The bet against a meeting firmed as Iran claimed a strike on a Bahrain air base and reports said it plotted a dirty bomb against Trump officials, then held as supertankers hit mines in Hormuz. Doha's push to revive talks and Kushner's confirmation of meetings with Iranian officials, via Vance's channel, have not pulled it back.

poly-moodys-or-sp-downgrades-france-by-n.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Moody's or S&P cuts France's sovereign credit rating before its deadline. Those ratings feed into what Paris pays to borrow and which funds can hold its bonds.

poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.standing: A Polymarket contract on Iran formally quitting the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty by 2027. The treaty lets a member leave on three months' notice, and leaving would end the legal basis for inspections of Iran's sites.
poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.recent: The fall came as diplomacy reopened: Doha moved to revive Iran-US talks, and Jared Kushner confirmed meetings with Iranian officials through a channel run by Vice President Vance. In Tehran, a debate over nuclear doctrine drew the foreign minister's assurance that the 60% uranium stockpile stays home, even as Iran tightened its grip on Hormuz.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027; its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. It asks about an invasion, a far higher bar than an air or missile strike.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Iran kept up strikes on Bahrain and mines in Hormuz, but a negotiating track opened alongside them. Doha moved to revive Iran-US talks, and Jared Kushner confirmed meetings with Iranian officials through a channel run by Vice President Vance, while Trump kept 'all options on the table'. In Israel, Avigdor Liberman said there were no grounds to strike Iran now.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States ends its blockade of Iran by the close of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which is tied to whether Gulf oil reaches its importers.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: The slide came as the standoff hardened: a third US carrier reached the Gulf, Iran struck a Bahraini industrial site, and its navy said two supertankers hit mines in Hormuz, where crossings fell more than 40% in three weeks. Since then Qatar has pressed to revive talks, and Jared Kushner confirmed meetings with Iranian officials.

poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Israel-Hamas ceasefire is cancelled by Dec 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reacts to fighting in Gaza and to the politics of the governments behind the truce.
poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.recent: Israel moved the yellow line again on 25 October, then launched central Gaza's first large operation since the ceasefire, and the Board of Peace warned the truce faced imminent collapse. Neither side has called it off: the strikes have run inside the ceasefire rather than ending it.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its December meeting. That rate anchors short-term dollar borrowing, so bonds, mortgages and currencies worldwide reprice around it.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, beating forecasts, and the Fed's minutes then showed almost all officials expecting more rate hikes. Goolsbee left a larger rise open, but CME FedWatch put a half-point move at zero, leaving the quarter point as the bet, and the Bureau of Economic Analysis then put inflation at 3.8%.

poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Ukraine signs its EU accession treaty by 2027. Signing comes only after every negotiating chapter closes and all 27 member states agree, so the price is a bet on the pace of talks in Brussels.
poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.recent: Bets slid as Washington set January 2027 as its deadline for a Ukraine peace deal, putting the war's end ahead of any treaty. EU leaders then stalled on their budget and on a €45 billion loan Ukraine would repay only if Russia pays reparations. Hungary's prime minister, Magyar, came to Uzhhorod with generators, not weapons.

poly-pete-hegseth-out-as-secretary-of-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Hegseth stops being the US Secretary of Defense before the end of the year. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on reports about his standing at the Pentagon.

wiki-inflation.standing: The general rise in prices across an economy, usually measured by a consumer price index. Central banks set interest rates to keep it near a target, so its pace decides what borrowers and savers pay.
wiki-inflation.recent: Late November brought a run of fresh price figures: US inflation hit 3.8% in October, Australian inflation reached 4.9% despite 125 basis points of hikes, Tokyo core prices rose 2.9%, and food prices in Sudan rose 15.27% in October alone. None of it dates from the early-November days the series moved.

wiki-china.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on China each day: a rough gauge of how often the world's second-largest economy and most populous one-party state pulls general readers toward the basics.
wiki-china.recent: Trump met Putin and Xi in Shenzhen at a summit billed as a peace treaty and likened to Yalta, while Putin vowed 'much more painful' strikes on Ukraine. Days later Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining, a Politburo member, came under investigation, and Solomon Islands moved to quit its 2022 China security pact.

poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Houthis and Saudi Arabia agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders will pay on the war between Yemen's Houthi movement and the kingdom ending, and so on Red Sea and Gulf oil risk.
poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.recent: Houthi missile debris fell on Riyadh as Houthi forces advanced on Aden, and the Saudi coalition hit 60 Houthi military sites. The Houthis then claimed strikes on a Saudi power plant and the Ras Tanura refinery and ordered Jeddah's port evacuated, and the Makkah pact now meets in Islamabad on the war.

poly-will-bola-tinubu-win-the-2027-niger.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Bola Tinubu wins Nigeria's 2027 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay on a second term for the president of Africa's most populous country.
poly-will-bola-tinubu-win-the-2027-niger.recent: Nigeria's electoral commission blamed 54 officials for fake voter records, Tinubu told Oyo voters in Ibadan that the pain of reform will pay, and the naira fell 3.6% this month to 1,403.50 per dollar as investors grew wary of an election upset. None of it lines up with a turn in the price.

stocks:MSFT.standing: Shares in the maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, one of the world's most valuable companies. Its OpenAI stake and its data-centre spending make it a bellwether for whether the AI build-out pays.
stocks:MSFT.recent: A 24-hour failure of Outlook, Teams and Microsoft 365 hit governments in Canada, the US, Australia and Japan, and the shares fell 3% as it ran. A researcher leaked SignDrop, a Windows exploit handing ordinary users System rights, the same week, and Microsoft has since declared an internal Code Red that puts reliability first.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Israel-Iran ceasefire is still holding on 31 December. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on every strike, threat and report of talks.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Avigdor Liberman said Israel has no grounds to strike Iran now and doubted the chemical-weapons claim offered as one. Diplomacy moved in parallel: Doha is reviving Iran-US talks, and Jared Kushner confirmed meetings with Iranian officials under a channel run by Vice President Vance.

wiki-nvidia.standing: Nvidia, the Santa Clara chip designer whose graphics processors run most of the world's AI training, and one of the most valuable companies on earth. Its fortunes carry the chip sector and the data-centre build-out with them.
wiki-nvidia.recent: Jensen Huang fell from Nvidia in mid-November, and the company went on to forecast a $130bn quarter without him. The board then reinstated him and the stock rose nearly 31%. Days later Nvidia stopped server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as Washington pursued chip diversion through firms like Megaspeed.

poly-will-pete-hegseth-be-the-first-of-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US House of Representatives impeaches Pete Hegseth, the defense secretary, before 2028. Impeachment takes only a simple House majority, so the price lives on who controls the chamber.
poly-will-pete-hegseth-be-the-first-of-t.recent: The window spans the U.S. midterm election, but nothing here says how its result reached Hegseth. The one prediction-market story it carries is Trump Jr. leaving Kalshi after his firm's $300 million investment in Polymarket, and that does not account for the price.

stocks:SPCX.standing: The rocket and satellite company Elon Musk founded. It flies most of the world's orbital launches and runs Starlink, the largest satellite internet network, and its military Starshield variant makes it a defence contractor too.
stocks:SPCX.recent: SpaceX's tower caught Ship 42 after 14 orbits, the first catch of a Starship upper stage. The FCC then licensed up to 1 million SpaceX satellites, and Virginia and Oregon sued over sexualised images posted by Grok. All of it came after the slide from late October into early November, and none of it explains that fall.

poly-us-strike-on-cuba-by-december-31.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States carries out a military strike on Cuba before its deadline. Its price is what traders stake on open conflict between Washington and Havana, 90 miles apart across the Florida Straits.
poly-us-strike-on-cuba-by-december-31.recent: Trump said in mid-November that he would consider military force against Cuba, the one statement on a strike the fortnight carried. No report since has turned that remark into an order or a deployment, and none explains why traders now pay less for a strike.

stocks:BABA.standing: The Hangzhou group behind Taobao and Tmall, China's biggest online marketplaces, and the country's largest cloud computing business. These New York-listed shares trade on Chinese consumer spending and its bets on artificial intelligence.
stocks:BABA.recent: Alibaba's own news in the window was expansion: plans to list its T-Head chip unit in Hong Kong while keeping control, with over 60% of T-Head's computing serving outside customers, and an AI music app. Neither accounts for the fall. The US export blacklisting of its Apex unit, alongside 6 other firms, came only after the slide.

poly-iaea-visits-isfahan-fordow-or-natan.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors visit an Iranian nuclear site by the year's end. Those inspections are the only outside check on how much enriched uranium Iran holds.
poly-iaea-visits-isfahan-fordow-or-natan.recent: The UN watchdog called on Iran to reopen its nuclear facilities to inspection. It conceded that its inspectors cannot reach the sites hit in the US-Israeli attacks and do not know where the Isfahan plant is. A week later Iran's foreign minister said its 60% uranium stockpile stays home.

poly-ukraine-signs-peace-deal-with-russi.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a peace deal before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on talks, battlefield turns and Washington's diplomacy.
poly-ukraine-signs-peace-deal-with-russi.recent: Washington's own timetable now runs past the contract's end: US officials say they want a deal by January 2027. Zelensky said the US had asked Ukraine to trade Donbas for NATO entry. Putin vowed 'much more painful' strikes, and Ukraine hit the Savasleyka airbase and sank the corvette Merkury.

poly-will-no-second-mandate-to-form-a-go.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the first lawmaker Israel's president asks to form a government after the 2026 vote succeeds, so that no second candidate is handed the mandate. Each failed round brings Israel closer to another election.
poly-will-no-second-mandate-to-form-a-go.recent: Likud and Yashar ended coalition talks on Nov 22 because Likud wanted Itamar Ben-Gvir in government and Yashar refused. Three days later Gadi Eisenkot signed his first partner, the left-wing Democrats, which gave his bloc 48 seats, 13 short of the 61 needed to oust Netanyahu.

stocks:AMZN.standing: The world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the biggest seller of cloud computing. AWS earns most of the company's operating profit, so the share moves on cloud demand as much as on shopping.
stocks:AMZN.recent: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan failed 10 minutes after liftoff and destroyed 40 Amazon Leo satellites, a fault ULA traced to its fuel supply rather than Blue Origin's engines. Amazon then moved Leo launches to its rival SpaceX, after an Ariane 6 lifted 36 more into orbit from Kourou.

stocks:DBK.DE.standing: Shares of Germany's largest lender, listed in Frankfurt and run with a large investment-banking arm. The price tracks European interest rates, trading income and the bank's legal and credit costs.
stocks:DBK.DE.recent: The shares fell on reports of a leak of 15 million internal files showing the bank kept about 28,000 flagged clients, and that a May 2020 memo tied two Trump companies to laundromats. Later files showed compliance staff softening slave-labour allegations against Cutrale and keeping BRF as a client despite rating it high-risk.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: The English Wikipedia article on artificial intelligence: software that learns from data to reason, write, see and act. How many open it each day shows how far the subject reaches beyond the people building it.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: The fortnight's AI story was a market reversal.
